article.headline: Milwaukee Brewers Storm to 3-0 World Series Lead Over Tampa Bay Rays
article.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers move one win away from their first championship after a 10-1 Game 3 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays.
article.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers turned a fifth-inning challenge into a historic rout at Tropicana Field, scoring eight two-out runs in a 10-1 victory that pushed the Tampa Bay Rays to the brink of elimination. After a successful replay review overturned a call at second base, Milwaukee became the first team to record seven consecutive hits in a postseason game. This offensive surge leaves Milwaukee just one win shy of securing the first championship in franchise history.

The Brewers' dominance has been absolute, as they remain undefeated since October 6. For Tampa Bay, the situation is grim; no team has ever forced a sixth game in a World Series after trailing 3-0 in the best-of-seven series. Milwaukee’s pitching staff has consistently outperformed the Rays, while Tampa Bay’s own starters have struggled to a 6.77 ERA throughout the first three games.

Following the loss, Milwaukee players emphasized a focus on maintaining their momentum, with Sal Frelick noting that the team continues to play until the series is officially decided. Conversely, Tampa Bay designated hitter Yandy Díaz acknowledged the difficulty of the deficit but insisted the team must look ahead to the next game to keep their championship hopes alive.

With the Brewers leading the series 3-0, the pressure on Tampa Bay is immense. As history shows, only one team in any best-of-seven postseason series has managed to overcome such a deficit. The Rays now prepare for Game 4, knowing that a single loss will end their season and mark the first World Series sweep since 2012.

article.headline: Milwaukee Brewers One Win From Historic Sweep After Dominating Rays In Game 3
article.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers hold a 3-0 World Series lead over the Tampa Bay Rays entering Tuesday's Game 4 at Tropicana Field.
article.body:
Milwaukee’s relentless offense put the Rays on the brink of elimination in Game 3, shattering records with eight two-out runs in a single inning to secure a lopsided 10-1 victory. The Brewers, who have yet to drop a game in the Fall Classic, now stand just one win away from becoming the first franchise in Major League Baseball history to sweep both a best-of-seven League Championship Series and the World Series in the same postseason. Brewers second baseman Brice Turang emphasized the team's urgency to finish the job, noting that players are committed to competing as hard as possible to maintain their pressure on Tampa Bay.

The stakes for Game 4 reach a historical threshold, as the Rays attempt a comeback that almost no team has ever achieved. According to MLB.com, teams trailing 3-0 in best-of-seven series have lost the series 42 out of 43 times. While the 2004 Red Sox famously overcame a 3-0 deficit in the American League Championship Series against the Yankees, no team has ever successfully forced a Game 6 after trailing 3-0 in the World Series. 

Behind the Brewers' success is a philosophy rooted in internal development and roster turnover, exemplified by the performance of rookie pitcher Robert Gasser. Analysts Jordan Shusterman and Jake Mintz pointed to the contrast between Milwaukee's reliance on emerging arms and the Rays' reliance on veteran ace Freddy Peralta. Despite defensive struggles and the weight of a 3-0 series hole, Rays players like Yandy Díaz maintained that their focus remains entirely on winning the next game to extend the series. The matchup continues Tuesday night in St. Petersburg, where the Brewers look to cement their title run.

article.headline: Aaron Ashby Sets Historic Postseason Scoreless Record During Brewers World Series Loss
article.summary: Aaron Ashby established a new MLB record for consecutive scoreless innings by a reliever in a single postseason during Tuesday's 4-3 defeat to the Tampa Bay Rays.
article.body:
Aaron Ashby sprinted past Andrew Miller’s record by delivering 2 1/3 perfect innings during Game 4 of the World Series on Tuesday night. By retiring seven consecutive batters after entering in the ninth inning at Tropicana Field, Ashby extended his dominant postseason streak to 18 total frames, according to the Elias Sports Bureau. This feat solidifies his status as the only pitcher in history to record at least five outs in six or more consecutive postseason appearances without allowing a single run.

For the Brewers, Ashby’s performance has been the backbone of their late-season success. Following a career path that once included shoulder surgery and a stint at Triple-A Nashville, the left-hander has transformed into a high-leverage relief ace. This reliability has allowed manager Pat Murphy to utilize him frequently, often calling upon him for multiple innings on consecutive nights to keep the team’s championship hopes alive.

Despite Ashby’s historic performance on Tuesday, which sent the game into extra innings, the Brewers ultimately fell 4-3 to the Rays in 12 frames. While the Brewers led in the 12th after a solo home run by Cooper Pratt, Tampa Bay successfully rallied to win the game. The result forces a Game 5 between the two clubs on Wednesday.

Ashby’s streak now surpasses the 16-inning single-postseason record previously held by Andrew Miller, who set the mark while playing for Cleveland in 2016. Reflecting on the achievement, Miller told 620 WTMJ that he was not concerned about losing the record, instead praising Ashby for his crucial role as the team's "glue guy" during this postseason run.

news.title: Mortgage Rates Hold Steady Yet Again
news.og_title: Mortgage Rates Hold Steady Yet Again
news.og_desc: It was a remarkably calm day for the mortgage market on two separate levels. First off, the average lender set this morning's rates right in line with yesterday's latest levels. Additionally, there were very few intraday changes (and in those cases, rates improved modestly).  [thirtyyearmortgagerates]  All of the above is made possible by the fact that the bond market stayed right in line with yesterday's levels all day long. This has happened for two straight days now, and it's the sort of stability that seemed like a distant memory several weeks ago.  Will it last?  There's never any way to know for sure. The bond/rate market is constantly at risk of responding to several sources of motivation. It just so happens that those sources have been silent after last week's improvement.&nbsp;  It's worth noting that there's a new Fed rate announcement tomorrow. Fed announcements often create volatility for rates and that volatility is rarely related to whether the Fed hikes/cuts/holds steady. In tomorrow's case, we already have a high degree of certainty that the Fed will not be hiking rates. Any impact the Fed has on mortgage rates would be a factor of the words they use in the policy statement or the words spoken by Fed Chair Warsh in the 2:30pm ET press conference.&nbsp;  Beyond the Fed, there are still other potential considerations for rates (tech sector volatility, war-related headlines), but never any guarantee that they'll adhere to a certain timeline.&nbsp;
